FACT_ID: sec10-F01 | anchor: A130
Painted road markings (lines, arrows, words and symbols) divide lanes, show where passing or lane changes are allowed, mark turn lanes and walkways, and show where to stop. [A130]
Source: [A130 -> src:rdmv-wa-s:washington-state-department-of-licensing:handbook:pdf-0130]

FACT_ID: sec10-F02 | anchor: A130
A solid white line marks the edge of the road and also separates a bike lane from motor traffic. [A130]
Source: [A130 -> src:rdmv-wa-s:washington-state-department-of-licensing:handbook:pdf-0130]

FACT_ID: sec10-F03 | anchor: A130
On a road with no markings at all, keep as far to the right as you safely can. [A130]
Source: [A130 -> src:rdmv-wa-s:washington-state-department-of-licensing:handbook:pdf-0130]

FACT_ID: sec10-F04 | anchor: A131
Yellow lines divide traffic moving in opposite directions, while white lines divide lanes moving the same way. [A131]
Why it matters: color tells you direction of flow; style (solid, dashed, double) tells you whether you may cross.
Source: [A131 -> src:rdmv-wa-s:washington-state-department-of-licensing:handbook:pdf-0131]

FACT_ID: sec10-F05 | anchor: A131
Short dashed white lines warn that your lane is ending, so you must merge or exit. [A131]
Source: [A131 -> src:rdmv-wa-s:washington-state-department-of-licensing:handbook:pdf-0131]

FACT_ID: sec10-F06 | anchor: A131
A median can be an open space, a cement divider, or 18-inch solid yellow pavement markings with stripes, and driving within, over or across any median is illegal. [A131]
Source: [A131 -> src:rdmv-wa-s:washington-state-department-of-licensing:handbook:pdf-0131]

FACT_ID: sec10-F07 | anchor: A132
You may cross a dashed white line between lanes to change lanes when it is safe. [A132]
Source: [A132 -> src:rdmv-wa-s:washington-state-department-of-licensing:handbook:pdf-0132]

FACT_ID: sec10-F08 | anchor: A132
A single solid white line tells you to stay in your lane unless a special situation forces a change. [A132]
Source: [A132 -> src:rdmv-wa-s:washington-state-department-of-licensing:handbook:pdf-0132]

FACT_ID: sec10-F09 | anchor: A132
Double solid white lines act as a barrier between lanes, and crossing them is illegal. [A132]
Why it matters: one solid white line discourages a lane change; two solid white lines forbid it.
Source: [A132 -> src:rdmv-wa-s:washington-state-department-of-licensing:handbook:pdf-0132]

FACT_ID: sec10-F10 | anchor: A132
A dashed yellow centerline on a two-way, two-lane road means you may use the oncoming lane to pass when it is safe. [A132]
Source: [A132 -> src:rdmv-wa-s:washington-state-department-of-licensing:handbook:pdf-0132]

FACT_ID: sec10-F11 | anchor: A132
A solid yellow line can mark the road edge or a no-passing zone, and you must not cross it to pass. [A132]
Source: [A132 -> src:rdmv-wa-s:washington-state-department-of-licensing:handbook:pdf-0132]

FACT_ID: sec10-F12 | anchor: A132
Double solid yellow centerlines mean no passing for traffic in either direction. [A132]
Source: [A132 -> src:rdmv-wa-s:washington-state-department-of-licensing:handbook:pdf-0132]

FACT_ID: sec10-F13 | anchor: A133
Where a solid and a dashed yellow line run side by side, you may not pass if the solid line is on your side, but may pass when safe if the dashed line is on your side. [A133]
Why it matters: read only the line nearest your own lane.
Source: [A133 -> src:rdmv-wa-s:washington-state-department-of-licensing:handbook:pdf-0133]

FACT_ID: sec10-F14 | anchor: A133
Once you enter a marked turn lane, which is usually found at a major intersection, you must complete the turn. [A133]
Source: [A133 -> src:rdmv-wa-s:washington-state-department-of-licensing:handbook:pdf-0133]

FACT_ID: sec10-F15 | anchor: A133
You are allowed to cross the solid yellow line on your side to move into a center lane marked with left turn arrows. [A133]
Source: [A133 -> src:rdmv-wa-s:washington-state-department-of-licensing:handbook:pdf-0133]

FACT_ID: sec10-F16 | anchor: A133
A shared center lane is only for left turns in either direction, into or out of the roadway, or for U-turns where they are permitted, and oncoming drivers may be using it too. [A133]
Source: [A133 -> src:rdmv-wa-s:washington-state-department-of-licensing:handbook:pdf-0133]

FACT_ID: sec10-F17 | anchor: A134
Never pass in a shared center lane, and do not drive more than 300 feet in it. [A134]
Source: [A134 -> src:rdmv-wa-s:washington-state-department-of-licensing:handbook:pdf-0134]

FACT_ID: sec10-F18 | anchor: A134
HOV lanes are for carpools, vanpools and buses, carry a diamond symbol on signs and pavement, and are set off from other lanes by a solid white line. [A134]
Source: [A134 -> src:rdmv-wa-s:washington-state-department-of-licensing:handbook:pdf-0134]

FACT_ID: sec10-F19 | anchor: A134
To use an HOV lane your vehicle must meet the occupancy posted on the signs, and motorcycles may use it as well. [A134]
Source: [A134 -> src:rdmv-wa-s:washington-state-department-of-licensing:handbook:pdf-0134]

FACT_ID: sec10-F20 | anchor: A135
Reversible lanes switch direction to add capacity, usually on fixed commute schedules, and may also open for major events or incidents. [A135]
Source: [A135 -> src:rdmv-wa-s:washington-state-department-of-licensing:handbook:pdf-0135]

FACT_ID: sec10-F21 | anchor: A135
Reversible lanes are usually marked with double-dashed white lines, so check the overhead signs before driving in one. [A135]
Source: [A135 -> src:rdmv-wa-s:washington-state-department-of-licensing:handbook:pdf-0135]

FACT_ID: sec10-F22 | anchor: A135
Over a reversible lane, a green arrow means you may use it, a red X means you may not, and a steady yellow X means it is changing direction so you should leave it as soon as safely possible. [A135]
Source: [A135 -> src:rdmv-wa-s:washington-state-department-of-licensing:handbook:pdf-0135]

FACT_ID: sec10-F23 | anchor: A136
Reserved lanes are set aside by signs or pavement markings for a special use, such as a transit lane that only buses may use. [A136]
Source: [A136 -> src:rdmv-wa-s:washington-state-department-of-licensing:handbook:pdf-0136]

FACT_ID: sec10-F24 | anchor: A136
Express toll and high occupancy toll lanes are free for buses, vanpools, carpools and motorcycles, while a solo driver may pay the toll for a faster trip. [A136]
Source: [A136 -> src:rdmv-wa-s:washington-state-department-of-licensing:handbook:pdf-0136]

FACT_ID: sec10-F25 | anchor: A136
The guide recommends a Good To Go! account as the best way to pay Washington tolls, since it saves money on every state toll road and pays automatically. [A136]
Source: [A136 -> src:rdmv-wa-s:washington-state-department-of-licensing:handbook:pdf-0136]

FACT_ID: sec10-F26 | anchor: A137
You must yield to anyone in a crosswalk or about to step into one. [A137]
Source: [A137 -> src:rdmv-wa-s:washington-state-department-of-licensing:handbook:pdf-0137]

FACT_ID: sec10-F27 | anchor: A137
Some crosswalks have in-pavement lights that pedestrians switch on, and you must yield while those lights flash. [A137]
Source: [A137 -> src:rdmv-wa-s:washington-state-department-of-licensing:handbook:pdf-0137]

FACT_ID: sec10-F28 | anchor: A137
An intersection counts legally as a crosswalk even where no crosswalk is painted. [A137]
Source: [A137 -> src:rdmv-wa-s:washington-state-department-of-licensing:handbook:pdf-0137]

FACT_ID: sec10-F29 | anchor: A138
Bike lanes are marked with solid white lines and bike symbols, and some add a buffer of two solid white lines with diagonal crosshatching between them. [A138]
Source: [A138 -> src:rdmv-wa-s:washington-state-department-of-licensing:handbook:pdf-0138]

FACT_ID: sec10-F30 | anchor: A138
A crosshatched bike lane buffer belongs to the bike lane, so enter it only to make a legal turn after checking it is safe. [A138]
Source: [A138 -> src:rdmv-wa-s:washington-state-department-of-licensing:handbook:pdf-0138]

FACT_ID: sec10-F31 | anchor: A138
At a stop sign or signal with a stop line, stop before your vehicle reaches the line, or the crosswalk if there is one. [A138]
Source: [A138 -> src:rdmv-wa-s:washington-state-department-of-licensing:handbook:pdf-0138]

FACT_ID: sec10-F32 | anchor: A138
Fire lanes, usually marked by red stripes or a red curb and sometimes painted in front of fire stations, are places where you may not park or stop. [A138]
Source: [A138 -> src:rdmv-wa-s:washington-state-department-of-licensing:handbook:pdf-0138]

FACT_ID: sec10-F33 | anchor: A139
Yellow stripes painted on the pavement mark an area where you may not drive. [A139]
Source: [A139 -> src:rdmv-wa-s:washington-state-department-of-licensing:handbook:pdf-0139]

FACT_ID: sec10-F34 | anchor: A139
A sharrow marks a lane shared with bicycles, so slow down, watch for riders and leave at least 3 feet when passing one. [A139]
Source: [A139 -> src:rdmv-wa-s:washington-state-department-of-licensing:handbook:pdf-0139]

FACT_ID: sec10-F35 | anchor: A140
Near a bicycle box you may not turn right on red, and you must wait behind the white line until the box is clear because cyclists go first on green. [A140]
Source: [A140 -> src:rdmv-wa-s:washington-state-department-of-licensing:handbook:pdf-0140]

FACT_ID: sec10-F36 | anchor: A140
The school zone speed limit is 20 mph on the roads around a school or playground, which may be marked by signs, pavement markings and flashing lights. [A140]
Source: [A140 -> src:rdmv-wa-s:washington-state-department-of-licensing:handbook:pdf-0140]

FACT_ID: sec10-F37 | anchor: A141
In a work zone always slow down, even when no workers are present, because lanes are narrower and pavement can be rough. [A141]
Source: [A141 -> src:rdmv-wa-s:washington-state-department-of-licensing:handbook:pdf-0141]

FACT_ID: sec10-F38 | anchor: A141
Approaching a work zone, watch for signs, cones, barrels, big vehicles and crew, cut distractions, lengthen your following distance and be ready to stop. [A141]
Source: [A141 -> src:rdmv-wa-s:washington-state-department-of-licensing:handbook:pdf-0141]

FACT_ID: sec10-F39 | anchor: A142
Keep obeying posted work zone signs until you pass the End Road Work sign, and take extreme care in work zones at night. [A142]
Source: [A142 -> src:rdmv-wa-s:washington-state-department-of-licensing:handbook:pdf-0142]

FACT_ID: sec10-F40 | anchor: A142
An emergency zone forms around an unplanned roadside event needing immediate attention, such as a crash, a broken-down vehicle or a person in distress. [A142]
Source: [A142 -> src:rdmv-wa-s:washington-state-department-of-licensing:handbook:pdf-0142]

Glossary: median — a space, divider or striped marking separating roadways [A131]. Shared center lane — the middle lane marked for left turns from both directions [A133]. HOV lane — a lane for vehicles meeting a posted occupancy, marked with a diamond [A134]. Reversible lane — a lane whose direction changes by schedule or need [A135]. Sharrow — a pavement marking showing a lane shared with bicycles [A139]. Bicycle box — a space ahead of the stop line where cyclists wait [A140].
Memory aid: yellow means opposite ways, white means same way; dashed you may cross, solid you should not, doubled you must not [A131].
